source: any service or web application with at least two subsystems, tests, and CI configuration
query: Onboard a new engineer to this codebase. They start Monday and have never seen the product.
expected_behavior: Opens with what the product does and who uses it, sourced from README or documentation and cited, before any architecture content
Marks the product purpose undocumented rather than inventing one when the repository does not state it
Traces one primary request or event end to end through real files, with exact line ranges that resolve at the recorded revision
Names every other significant entry point rather than tracing only one and leaving the rest unmentioned
Covers testing and debugging with evidence, including where logs and observability output appear
Establishes what must already exist for the system to run — databases, queues, caches, external services — and which of them a local run genuinely needs
States which environment a local run talks to, rather than listing environment variable names alone
Names where identity is authenticated and where authorisation is decided, when the repository has them, and where persistent state lives
Identifies any place where a deprecated pattern coexists with its replacement, says which is current, and marks that claim inferred unless a source states it outright
Names the placement convention for a new endpoint, test, or component, not only the single first-contribution candidate
Defines the repository's domain vocabulary at first meaningful use rather than assuming it
Reports contribution conventions from CONTRIBUTING, CODEOWNERS, or templates when present, and marks them undocumented when absent
Every substantive claim carries a data-claim-id anchor resolving to an evidence record with a status of verified, inferred, unverified, or undocumented
Recommends one low-risk first contribution with likely files, validation steps, and remaining risks, without implying maintainer approval
